How a project runs

  1. Workshop

    We map your goals, users and constraints, and find the few XR ideas that are actually worth building.

  2. Prototype

    A working prototype you can put on a headset or open from a link, tested with real users early.

  3. Production

    Design, development and testing through to launch, in WebXR or as a native headset app where that is the better choice.

  4. Rollout

    Hardware, distribution, onboarding and measurement, so the experience gets used and not just launched.

Why WebXR is often the smartest choice

Most immersive projects lose their audience at the app store. WebXR runs straight in the headset browser, so an experience is one link away: no download, no account, no review queue. That makes it faster to ship, cheaper to update and far easier to share. Morten has built one of the largest WebXR platforms, so he knows when the web is the right call and when a native app is.

Frequently asked

What does an XR consultant do?

An XR consultant helps an organisation decide where virtual, augmented and mixed reality can create value, chooses the right technology and hardware, and guides or delivers the build. Morten covers the whole chain, from strategy workshop to shipped product.

What is the difference between VR, AR, MR and XR?

Virtual reality (VR) replaces your surroundings with a digital world. Augmented reality (AR) places digital content on top of the real world. Mixed reality (MR) lets digital objects interact with your real room. Extended reality (XR) is the umbrella term for all three.

Which headset should we choose?

It depends on your users, budget, content and IT requirements. Meta Quest is the most widespread standalone headset, Apple Vision Pro leads on display quality, and smart glasses suit lightweight, everyday use. A short workshop is the quickest way to get a clear answer.

Do you work outside Denmark?

Yes. Morten is based in Copenhagen and works with clients across Europe, in English or Danish.
